name: tao-trader (lean): one loop, four seams, snapshot-driven
philosophy:
THESIS
The research brief says most things you could build here lose money: passive price-only micro-cap longs (gate-era SMB about -0.5%/day), seeded launches (median -68% to -74% by day 90, 0 of 11 positive), anything held through a prune (0.35-0.65x spot). The only structural positives are 1-day continuation and 7-day momentum (gross of costs) and nominator yield (+0.3-0.6%/day on micro caps, with the net total-return sign unknown). So this system is a falsification machine first and a trader second. Its job is to answer, cheaply and honestly, "does anything survive total return (price x share-price index), own impact, fees, prune risk and regime splits?" "Hold TAO" is a legitimate, reportable result and sits in every comparison table. Outputs describe what backtests and paper trading show; nothing here is personalised investment advice.

ONE IDEA
State is a ChainSnapshot: block, globals, and about 128 SubnetStates keyed by (netuid, NetworkRegisteredAt). Everything else is a pure function of snapshots.
  events   = diff(prev, cur)                    no event bus, no System.Events decoding
  features = f(snapshot, small rolling buffers) computed once per snapshot, shared by every book
  decision = allocate(signals) -> risk -> plan   pure functions
  money    = apply_fill / settle_dereg / mark    pure functions
Backtest, paper, live-dry and live run the SAME loop (engine.run). They differ in exactly two objects: the DataSource (ParquetReplay | LiveChain) and the ExecutionVenue (SimVenue | SimVenue on the live feed | LiveVenue). If a behaviour passes its tests with those two swapped, the only backtest-to-live skew left is the fill model, and that is bracketed and measured (see backtest_engine).

FOUR SEAMS, EVERYTHING ELSE IS FUNCTIONS
Protocols exist only where substitution really happens: DataSource, Strategy, RiskOverlay, ExecutionVenue. Everything else is a frozen dataclass or a module-level function. No plugin registry (strategies are named in TOML and imported), no ORM, no DI container, no pandas, no pydantic, no message queue, no second process. Runtime dependencies: websockets, httpx, xxhash, duckdb, numpy. Everything else is stdlib (asyncio, sqlite3, tomllib, hashlib, logging, argparse). The live extra adds bittensor==11.3.0 (hash-pinned) and is imported by exactly one module, live/venue.py.

COMPETE WITHOUT A FRAMEWORK
A Book is (strategy sleeves, risk overlay, venue, portfolio). One pass over the data drives N books. The competition table is every strategy family alone, a blended book, and the baselines (cash, equal-weight price-only, equal-weight with yield), each also run under both impact assumptions. That is about 24 books in one pass, with no extra machinery.

CORRECTNESS FIRST: WHAT MUST BE EXACT
Reader and decoders, the AMM, the emission-share function, the prune rule, the yield index, the era mapping, and the fill model's own footprint. I checked each against the live chain in this design pass (extra verification beyond the brief; read-only public RPC at OnFinality, block about 9,242,150, plus historical blocks 7,000,020 and 8,500,040-8,500,340):
 1. Key hashing: twox128("System") = 26aa394e...cef7 (brief's check value) and Timestamp.Now match.
 2. One state_queryStorageAt with 2,732 keys decodes all 128 subnets: 255 KiB in 0.40 s. Spec 475, LastRateLimitedBlock(0x02)=9,210,610, NetworkLastLockCost 653.02, gate bar 0.008248, TaoWeight 0.18, emission-disabled {29,35,36,82,108,116}, never-started {59,82,86}. All equal the brief.
 3. Pool price vs SwapRuntimeApi_current_alpha_price_all, all 128 subnets: worst relative error 8.8e-7 (rao quantisation).
 4. amm.buy vs SwapRuntimeApi_sim_swap_tao_for_alpha, SN1 with 1 TAO: alpha_out 152,285,961,807 and fee 503,547 rao, bit-exact.
 5. prune_target() vs SubnetInfoRuntimeApi_get_subnet_to_prune: SN92 live, and SN58 at historical block 8,500,160.
 6. emission_shares() vs SubnetTaoInEmission+SubnetExcessTao on all subnets: sum 0.5000 TAO/block, max error 0.002 TAO/day (SN51 473.05 vs 473.04). The Hill gate keeps only 0.2-2% of share on the smallest pools, so they receive about 0 emission.
 7. Yield: SN70 hotkey 56a9 has index I = 1.633188 and grew +0.553% in 24 h (brief closed form: 0.557%). The median of 49 earning hotkeys was 0.503%/day. The spread between hotkeys is only about 0.05%/day on SN70.
 8. Swap-v3 era (block 7,000,020, spec 348): constant product on virtual reserves (L*sqrtP, L/sqrtP) at weight 0.5, fed through the same amm.buy, matches sim_swap exactly on SN1, SN19, SN64 (and 2e-10 on SN100). Raw T/A is off by up to 0.03% on those pools. This resolves brief item 12: Swap.AlphaSqrtPrice is U64F64 under Twox64Concat, and Swap.CurrentLiquidity is a u64.
 9. Prune timing t* for ladder ranks 2-4 is 2.8 h, 4.8 h and 5.0 h (brief: 2.8 / 4.8 / 4.9-6.3); the closed form equals a brute-force EMA simulation (850 blocks).
10. Registration cost formula gives 962.89 TAO at block 9,240,878 (brief: 962.89).
11. A 6-block historical pull ran at 1.72 snapshots/s with a 3 req/s bucket (brief: 1.7/s), so Era C (about 12.6k snapshots at 60-block cadence) is roughly 2 h of collection.
12. Prototype core: about 1,000 lines. Eight test functions pass: AMM closed forms; the footprint bracket; dereg 0.417x spot; no-lookahead (future truncation); byte-identical determinism; data-cadence contract; regime guard; and a regression test for a real precedence bug I introduced and caught (a wake event could bypass a strategy's valid_from).

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT BUILD
No order-book or CEX layer, no ML or feature store, no scheduler framework, no web UI (reports are static HTML), no event bus, no System.Events decoder in v1 (events come from state diffs), no multi-process split, no generic plugin system, no metadata-driven SCALE codec at runtime. Each has a stated trigger for adding it (see tradeoffs).

HARD EDGES KEPT FROM THE USER'S DECISIONS
 - Live is gated and never self-arming. Bot key = zero-delay ProxyType::Staking only. No UnstakeAll, TransferStake or Batch intent is ever imported.
 - Capital is a config value. Sizing is pool-relative (a fraction of the effective pool TAO, plus an exit-slippage budget V <= T*s/(1-s)).
 - The Taostats MCP is for Claude-side research only. The bot uses chain reads plus optional Taostats REST enrichment (verification and trades), never in the decision path.
 - Windows runs the reader, collector, backtests and paper trader natively. Only the live adapter needs WSL2 or a Linux VPS.

"""tao_trader/types.py - every cross-module type. Frozen dataclasses, almost no behaviour."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import AsyncIterator, Literal, Mapping, NamedTuple, Protocol, Sequence

RAO = 10**9
FEE_DEN = 65_535
BLOCKS_PER_DAY = 7_200

# SubnetState.flags: why a number may be less trustworthy (reports can mask on these)
F_PRICE_TA = 1        # price from T/A (era A, or era B before first swap): biased for v3-era micro caps
F_SEED_FALLBACK = 2   # Balancer seeding fell back to q=0.5: check for a price jump
F_NO_YIELD_IDX = 4    # no tracked hotkey share-price index: nominator yield unknown
F_DEFAULTED = 8       # a ValueQuery item was filled from defaults.py on a spec whose defaults were not validated


class SubnetKey(NamedTuple):
    """One *generation* of a netuid. netuids are reused about weekly; never key on netuid alone."""
    netuid: int
    reg_at: int          # SubtensorModule.NetworkRegisteredAt


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- chain state
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class PoolState:
    tao: int                     # y in rao   (era B: virtual reserve L*sqrtP)
    alpha: int                   # x in rao   (era B: virtual reserve L/sqrtP)
    w_quote: float = 0.5         # TAO weight, Swap.SwapBalancer.quote/1e18 (0.5 in eras A/B)
    fee_rate: int = 33           # of 65535

    @property
    def spot(self) -> float:     # TAO per alpha
        return (1.0 - self.w_quote) / self.w_quote * self.tao / self.alpha


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class HotkeyIdx:
    """Share-price index I = TotalHotkeyAlpha / TotalHotkeyShares. A position holds shares, so yield accrues for free."""
    total_alpha: int
    total_shares: float          # SafeFloat / U64F64 decoded to float
    take: float = 0.18           # Delegates[h]/65535; 18% if the hotkey never set one
    earns: bool = True           # hotkey is a key of AlphaDividendsPerSubnet(netuid, .)

    @property
    def index(self) -> float:
        return self.total_alpha / self.total_shares if self.total_shares else 1.0


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SubnetState:
    key: SubnetKey
    pool: PoolState
    alpha_out: int               # SubnetAlphaOut (includes protocol + burned alpha)
    protocol_alpha: int
    ema: float                   # SubnetMovingPrice (drives emission share AND the prune rank)
    root_prop: float
    miner_burned: float
    emission_enabled: bool
    subtoken_enabled: bool       # False until the owner calls start_call: no buying
    first_emission_block: int | None
    tempo: int
    last_epoch_block: int
    tao_flow_cum: int | None     # SubnetTaoFlow running total (use deltas)
    escrow_alpha: int | None     # validator-basket alpha E, when known (forward-filled)
    hot: Mapping[str, HotkeyIdx] = field(default_factory=dict)   # tracked hotkeys only
    flags: int = 0
    reg_allowed: bool = True      # NetworkRegistrationAllowed: part of emission eligibility (False also freezes the EMA)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ChainGlobals:
    gate_bar: float              # EmissionGateBar (theta)
    gate_exponent: int
    tao_weight: float
    subnet_limit: int
    immunity: int
    reg_rate_limit: int
    last_reg_block: int          # LastRateLimitedBlock(NetworkLastRegistered)
    last_lock_cost: int          # NetworkLastLockCost, rao
    safe_mode_until: int
    moving_alpha: float          # SubnetMovingAlpha


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ChainSnapshot:
    block: int
    ts: int                      # unix seconds, from Timestamp.Now
    spec: int
    g: ChainGlobals
    subnets: Mapping[int, SubnetState]   # netuid -> state (current generation only)
    block_hash: str = ""

    def get(self, k: SubnetKey) -> SubnetState | None:
        s = self.subnets.get(k.netuid)
        return s if s is not None and s.key == k else None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- events (derived by diffing snapshots)
class EventKind(StrEnum):
    REGISTERED = "registered"
    DEREGISTERED = "deregistered"          # prune or dissolve; data["last"] = last SubnetState seen
    START_CALLED = "start_called"
    EMISSION_TOGGLED = "emission_toggled"  # data["enabled"]
    EPOCH_DRAIN = "epoch_drain"
    LARGE_FLOW = "large_flow"              # data["frac"] = net TAO flow / pool TAO
    SPEC_CHANGED = "spec_changed"
    PARAM_CHANGED = "param_changed"        # data["name"], ["old"], ["new"]
    CHAIN_ALERT = "chain_alert"            # stall, safe mode, reorg, rpc lag


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Event:
    kind: EventKind
    block: int
    key: SubnetKey | None = None
    data: Mapping[str, object] = field(default_factory=dict)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- decisions
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Signal:

    strategy: str
    key: SubnetKey
    edge_pd: float               # expected TAO-denominated return per day, net of dilution/take, before trading costs
    horizon_blocks: int          # amortises round-trip cost; also the signal's time-to-live unless refreshed
    conviction: float = 1.0      # 0..1
    hotkey: str | None = None    # preferred validator hotkey for nominator yield
    reason: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)

    block: int
    w: Mapping[SubnetKey, float]                 # fraction of NAV_liq per key; long-only; sum <= 1
    why: Mapping[SubnetKey, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    force_exit: frozenset[SubnetKey] = frozenset()   # flatten now: ignores hysteresis, uses urgent limits
    halt: str | None = None                      # no new risk (spec not accepted, stall, safe mode, drawdown)


Side = Literal["buy", "sell"]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OrderIntent:
    id: str
    key: SubnetKey
    side: Side
    hotkey: str
    amount: int                  # buy: gross TAO rao; sell: alpha rao (ignored when full_exit on a live venue)
    limit_price: float           # TAO/alpha bound on the pool's marginal spot AFTER the fill; strict
    allow_partial: bool
    full_exit: bool
    created_block: int
    ttl_blocks: int              # shielded eras are <= 8 blocks
    tag: str                     # strategy name, "risk_exit", "rebalance"


FillStatus = Literal["ok", "partial", "limit", "too_small", "pool_gone", "missed"]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Fill:
    order_id: str
    key: SubnetKey
    side: Side
    status: FillStatus
    block: int                   # inclusion block (N+2 for shielded)
    tao: int                     # buy: gross TAO paid (incl. swap fee); sell: TAO received
    alpha: int                   # buy: alpha received; sell: alpha sold
    shares: float                # hotkey-pool shares credited (buy) or debited (sell)
    swap_fee: int                # TAO-equivalent swap fee
    tx_fee: int                  # paid even when the inner call fails
    spot_before: float           # pool spot at fill time, for slippage attribution


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Position:
    key: SubnetKey
    hotkey: str
    shares: float
    cost_tao: float              # TAO paid incl. fees (attribution)
    entry_block: int
    strategy: str


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Portfolio:
    cash: int                    # free TAO in rao, fee reserve already excluded
    positions: Mapping[SubnetKey, Position] = field(default_factory=dict)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- derived features / risk views
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Feat:
    """Computed once per snapshot, shared by every book. None = not enough history."""
    spot: float
    ret_1d: float | None
    ret_7d: float | None
    ret_30d: float | None
    emis_tao_day: float          # re-implemented get_shares(): predicted TAO/day of emission
    gate_keep: float             # fraction of its burn-adjusted share that survives the Hill gate
    ema_rank: int                # 1 = largest burn-adjusted share
    yield_pd: float | None       # trailing realised d ln(index) per day of the best hotkey (already net of take)
    best_hotkey: str | None
    flow_frac_1d: float | None   # delta SubnetTaoFlow / pool TAO over 1 day
    dilution_pd: float           # protocol alpha minting per day / alpha_out
    escrow_frac: float | None    # basket E / pool alpha
    age_blocks: int
    since_start_blocks: int | None
    immune: bool
    prune_rank: int | None       # 1 = current prune target among non-immune subnets
    t_star_blocks: float | None  # blocks until this subnet could become the target if spot -> 0


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class PruneView:
    target: SubnetKey | None
    reg_open_at: int             # last_reg_block + reg_rate_limit: earliest next registration
    p_reg: Mapping[int, float]   # horizon blocks -> P(a registration lands), empirical CDF conditioned on elapsed time


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Context:
    raw: ChainSnapshot           # the market as it is: all FEATURES and signals come from here
    view: ChainSnapshot          # raw + this book's own footprint: all SIZING, QUOTES and MARKS come from here
    prev: ChainSnapshot | None
    events: Sequence[Event]
    feats: Mapping[SubnetKey, Feat]
    prune: PruneView
    port: Portfolio
    nav_liq: float               # TAO: cash + sell-quote of every position on `view`
    cfg: "BookCfg"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BookCfg:
    name: str
    capital_tao: float
    weights: Mapping[str, float]          # strategy name -> budget share (its sleeve)
    max_pool_frac: float = 0.01           # position <= 1% of effective pool TAO
    exit_slip_budget: float = 0.02        # position <= T*s/(1-s)
    max_names: int = 8
    gross_max: float = 0.95
    min_order_tao: float = 0.25           # fee amortisation floor (0.00103 TAO buy fee = 0.4% of 0.25)
    entry_hurdle: float = 0.02            # required net edge over the signal horizon (fraction)
    exit_hurdle: float = 0.0              # hysteresis: held names only need to clear this
    rebalance_band: float = 0.25
    decide_every_blocks: int = 60
    latency_blocks: int = 2


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- the four seams
class Strategy(Protocol):
    name: str
    decide_every: int                     # blocks between calls
    min_cadence: int                      # coarsest data cadence (blocks) this strategy tolerates; engine refuses coarser data
    valid_from: int                       # first block where its mechanism assumptions hold (regime guard)
    wake_on: frozenset[EventKind]         # events that trigger an early call
    def on_tick(self, ctx: Context) -> Sequence[Signal]: ...


class RiskOverlay(Protocol):
    def apply(self, tw: TargetWeights, ctx: Context) -> TargetWeights: ...


class ExecutionVenue(Protocol):
    mode: Literal["sim", "paper", "live_dry", "live"]
    def view(self, raw: ChainSnapshot) -> ChainSnapshot: ...         # raw + own footprint (identity when live)
    async def submit(self, orders: Sequence[OrderIntent], snap: ChainSnapshot) -> None: ...   # never blocks on a fill
    async def poll(self, snap: ChainSnapshot, held: Mapping[SubnetKey, Position]) -> list[Fill]: ...


class DataSource(Protocol):
    cadence_blocks: int                   # spacing of the snapshots this source yields
    def snapshots(self) -> AsyncIterator[ChainSnapshot]: ...
    async def aclose(self) -> None: ...

Design notes on the types
 - Position holds shares, not alpha. Value = shares x HotkeyIdx.index x pool price, so nominator yield accrues with no yield-specific code. Total return = price x index, as in the brief's identity. A buy at block B computes shares at the index visible in the snapshot that already contains any drain at or before B. That reproduces the on-chain rule that stake added in block B does not earn B's drain, and unstaking in B keeps the credit.
 - Context carries two snapshots on purpose. Features and signals read `raw` (the market). Sizing, quotes and marks read `view` (the market plus this book's own reserve footprint). A strategy therefore never mistakes its own impact for momentum.
 - Event is one class with a `kind` enum, not a class hierarchy; it maps straight to one row of the events table.
 - DataSource.cadence_blocks and Strategy.min_cadence form a data-resolution contract. The engine refuses to backtest a strategy that needs finer data than the source provides, so no result ever claims sub-snapshot reaction it cannot have.
 - Strategy.valid_from is a regime guard. The emission and gate mechanics only hold from block 8,765,684 (rank-32 gate), so strategies using them cannot run on earlier data. This is enforced in the engine, and a wake event cannot bypass it (regression-tested).
event_flow:
FLOW (identical in backtest, paper, live-dry and live). N books share one pass.

  DataSource.snapshots() --> raw ChainSnapshot
   1. events        = diff(prev, raw)                          pure; state diffs, no event decoding
   2. feats, prune  = FeatureEngine.update(raw, events)        once per snapshot, shared by all books
   per Book:
   3. view          = venue.view(raw)                          raw + own reserve footprint (identity when live)
   4. corporate actions: DEREGISTERED held key -> ledger.settle_dereg (cash credit), venue.forget
   5. fills         = venue.poll(view) -> ledger.apply_fill    sim: orders whose latency elapsed; live: reconcile carriers
   6. ctx           = Context(raw, view, prev, events, feats, prune, portfolio, nav_liq, cfg)
   7. strategies due (cadence elapsed OR a wake event, AND block >= valid_from) -> Signals, cached with TTL = horizon
   8. allocate(signals, ctx) -> TargetWeights                   strategy sleeves, net-edge hurdle, pool-relative caps
   9. risk.apply(tw, ctx)                                       final authority: force_exit, halt, caps
  10. plan(tw, ctx) -> OrderIntents                             limit prices, min sizes, dust rule, hotkey choice, one in flight per key
  11. venue.submit(orders)                                      async; the result arrives in a later poll()
  12. on_tick: RunStore.record / heartbeat / alerts             observes, never decides

CADENCE AND WAKE RULES
 - Decisions: each strategy declares decide_every (blocks) and wake_on (event kinds). Backtest default: one snapshot = 60 blocks, so a decision tick is every snapshot. Paper and live read every head (12 s) and diff every block, but run strategy code only on cadence or on a wake event (EPOCH_DRAIN, EMISSION_TOGGLED, REGISTERED, DEREGISTERED, LARGE_FLOW, SPEC_CHANGED, PARAM_CHANGED).
 - Risk tripwires and force_exit run on every snapshot, never gated by strategy cadence. A signal lives for its horizon_blocks unless the strategy refreshes it.
 - Signals are desired state, not trades. Allocation is hysteretic: entry needs net edge > entry_hurdle, a held name only needs > exit_hurdle. That removes churn without per-strategy state, and a restart needs only the portfolio plus the signal cache.
 - Honest limit: the backtest can only test reactions at the snapshot cadence. For sub-snapshot behaviour (prune reaction inside 12 min, emission-enable sniping), `collect --windows events.csv` pulls 5-block snapshots for roughly +/-4 h around known events (the 52 prunes in brief section 4.4, the 2026-06-22 purge block 8,463,544, the 2026-09-09 re-enable block 9,029,889). from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Mapping, Protocol, Sequence

from .events import diff
from .ledger import apply_fill, mark, settle_dereg
from .portfolio import allocate, plan
from .types import (BookCfg, Context, DataSource, EventKind, ExecutionVenue, Feat, Portfolio,
                    PruneView, RiskOverlay, Strategy, SubnetKey, ChainSnapshot, Event)


class Features(Protocol):
    warm: bool
    def update(self, raw: ChainSnapshot, events: Sequence[Event]) -> tuple[Mapping[SubnetKey, Feat], PruneView]: ...


@dataclass
class Book:
    cfg: BookCfg
    strategies: list[Strategy]
    risk: RiskOverlay
    venue: ExecutionVenue
    port: Portfolio
    dereg_fixed_frac: float | None = None           # None = formula; 0.35 / 0.65 = sensitivity runs
    sigs: dict = field(default_factory=dict)        # (strategy, key) -> (expires_block, Signal)
    last_call: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    orders: dict = field(default_factory=dict)      # in-flight order id -> OrderIntent
    log: list = field(default_factory=list)         # (block, nav_liq, [order ids], [fill statuses])
    seq: int = 0


async def step_book(b: Book, raw, prev, events, feats: Features, F, prune) -> None:
    view = b.venue.view(raw)
    pview = b.venue.view(prev) if prev is not None else None
    for ev in events:                                              # 1. corporate actions
        if ev.kind is EventKind.DEREGISTERED:
            if ev.key in b.port.positions:
                last = (pview.get(ev.key) if pview else None) or ev.data["last"]
                b.port = settle_dereg(b.port, ev.key, last, b.dereg_fixed_frac)
            b.venue.forget(ev.key) if hasattr(b.venue, "forget") else None
            b.orders = {i: o for i, o in b.orders.items() if o.key != ev.key}
    fills = await b.venue.poll(view, b.port.positions)             # 2. what resolved since last tick
    for f in fills:
        b.port = apply_fill(b.port, f, b.orders.pop(f.order_id))
    view = b.venue.view(raw)                                        # footprint changed by our fills
    nav = mark(b.port, view)[1]
    ctx = Context(raw, view, prev, events, F, prune, b.port, nav, b.cfg)
    if feats.warm:                                                  # 3. strategies on cadence or wake events
        for st in b.strategies:
            due = raw.block >= st.valid_from and (raw.block - b.last_call.get(st.name, -10**12) >= st.decide_every or any(
                e.kind in st.wake_on for e in events))
            if due:
                b.last_call[st.name] = raw.block
                for k in [k for k in b.sigs if k[0] == st.name]:
                    del b.sigs[k]                                   # a strategy's new opinion replaces its old one
                for sg in st.on_tick(ctx):
                    b.sigs[(sg.strategy, sg.key)] = (raw.block + sg.horizon_blocks, sg)
        live = [sg for exp, sg in b.sigs.values() if exp >= raw.block]
        tw = b.risk.apply(allocate(live, ctx), ctx)                 # 4. allocate -> risk (final authority)
        orders = plan(tw, ctx, {o.key for o in b.orders.values()}, b.seq)   # 5. plan
        b.seq += len(orders)
        await b.venue.submit(orders, view)                          # 6. execute (async; fills arrive via poll)
        for o in orders:
            b.orders[o.id] = o
    else:
        orders = []
    b.log.append((raw.block, round(nav, 9), [o.id for o in orders], [f.status for f in fills]))


async def run(source: DataSource, books: Sequence[Book], feats: Features, on_tick=None) -> None:
    check_contract(source, books)
    prev = None
    async for raw in source.snapshots():
        events = diff(prev, raw)                                    # pure
        F, prune = feats.update(raw, events)                        # once per snapshot, shared by every book
        for b in books:
            await step_book(b, raw, prev, events, feats, F, prune)
        if on_tick:
            await on_tick(raw, books, events)                       # persistence / heartbeat / alerts; never decides
        prev = raw
    await source.aclose()


def check_contract(source: DataSource, books: Sequence[Book]) -> None:
    """Refuse to backtest a strategy on data coarser than it can honestly react to."""
    for b in books:
        for st in b.strategies:
            if source.cadence_blocks > st.min_cadence:
                raise ValueError(f"{st.name} needs <= {st.min_cadence}-block data, source is {source.cadence_blocks}")

def diff(prev: ChainSnapshot | None, cur: ChainSnapshot, large_flow_frac: float = 0.02) -> list[Event]:
    if prev is None:
        return []
    ev: list[Event] = []
    b = cur.block
    if cur.spec != prev.spec:
        ev.append(Event(K.SPEC_CHANGED, b, None, {"old": prev.spec, "new": cur.spec}))
    for name in _GLOBAL_PARAMS:
        o, n = getattr(prev.g, name), getattr(cur.g, name)
        if o != n:
            ev.append(Event(K.PARAM_CHANGED, b, None, {"name": name, "old": o, "new": n}))
    pk = {s.key: s for s in prev.subnets.values()}
    ck = {s.key: s for s in cur.subnets.values()}
    for k in pk.keys() - ck.keys():                   # generation vanished: prune or dissolve (netuid reuse included)
        ev.append(Event(K.DEREGISTERED, b, k, {"last": pk[k]}))
    for k in ck.keys() - pk.keys():
        ev.append(Event(K.REGISTERED, b, k))
    for k in ck.keys() & pk.keys():
        a, n = pk[k], ck[k]
        if n.emission_enabled != a.emission_enabled:
            ev.append(Event(K.EMISSION_TOGGLED, b, k, {"enabled": n.emission_enabled}))
        if a.first_emission_block is None and n.first_emission_block is not None:
            ev.append(Event(K.START_CALLED, b, k))
        if n.last_epoch_block != a.last_epoch_block:
            ev.append(Event(K.EPOCH_DRAIN, b, k))
        if a.tao_flow_cum is not None and n.tao_flow_cum is not None and n.pool.tao:
            frac = (n.tao_flow_cum - a.tao_flow_cum) / n.pool.tao
            if abs(frac) >= large_flow_frac:
                ev.append(Event(K.LARGE_FLOW, b, k, {"frac": frac}))
    return ev

SWAP_FEE = 33 / 65_535
ROUND_TRIP_TX_TAO = 0.00186                    # 0.00103 buy + 0.00083 sell (brief 5.12)

def pool_cap_tao(s, max_pool_frac, slip):      # a fraction of the pool AND an exit-slippage budget, whichever binds first
    t = s.pool.tao / RAO
    return min(max_pool_frac * t, amm.v_max(t, slip))

def round_trip_cost(t, size):                  # pessimistic: other flow heals our footprint, so impact is paid on both legs
    return 2 * SWAP_FEE + ROUND_TRIP_TX_TAO / max(size, 1e-9) + 2 * size / (t + size)

def allocate(sigs, ctx) -> TargetWeights:
    """Strategy sleeves: each strategy owns weights[name] of gross and fills it with its own best net-edge names.
    Net edge = edge_pd x horizon - round-trip cost at the cap size. Held names need only clear exit_hurdle."""
    c = ctx.cfg
    by_strat = defaultdict(list)
    for sg in sigs: by_strat[sg.strategy].append(sg)
    w, why = defaultdict(float), {}
    nav = max(ctx.nav_liq, 1e-9)
    for name, group in by_strat.items():
        sleeve = c.weights.get(name, 0.0) * c.gross_max
        if sleeve <= 0: continue
        scored = []
        for sg in group:
            s = ctx.view.get(sg.key)
            if s is None or not s.subtoken_enabled: continue
            cap = pool_cap_tao(s, c.max_pool_frac, c.exit_slip_budget)
            size = min(cap, nav * sleeve)
            net = sg.edge_pd * sg.horizon_blocks / BLOCKS_PER_DAY * sg.conviction - round_trip_cost(s.pool.tao / RAO, size)
            hurdle = c.exit_hurdle if sg.key in ctx.port.positions else c.entry_hurdle
            if net > hurdle: scored.append((net, sg, cap))
        scored.sort(key=lambda t: -t[0])
        top = scored[: c.max_names]
        for _, sg, cap in top:
            w[sg.key] += min(sleeve / len(top), cap / nav)           # equal weight inside the sleeve, capped by depth
            why[sg.key] = f"{name}:{sg.reason}"
    for k in list(w):                                               # cross-sleeve cap
        w[k] = min(w[k], pool_cap_tao(ctx.view.get(k), c.max_pool_frac, c.exit_slip_budget) / nav)
    return TargetWeights(ctx.raw.block, dict(w), why)

def _buy_limit(p, tao_in, margin):   # marginal price after the fill: spot * (1 + dy/y)^(1/w_base), plus drift margin
    dy = tao_in - tao_in * p.fee_rate // 65_535
    return p.spot * (1.0 + dy / p.tao) ** (1.0 / (1.0 - p.w_quote)) * (1.0 + margin)

def _sell_limit(p, alpha, margin):
    dx = alpha - alpha * p.fee_rate // 65_535
    return p.spot * (1.0 + dx / p.alpha) ** (-1.0 / p.w_quote) * (1.0 - margin)

def pick_hotkey(s, preferred):       # among TRACKED hotkeys that earn: take 0 first, then the largest stake
    if preferred and preferred in s.hot: return preferred
    ok = [(h.take, -h.total_alpha, hk) for hk, h in s.hot.items() if h.earns]
    return min(ok)[2] if ok else None   # no tracked earning hotkey -> do not enter (yield and shares would be unknowable)

def plan(tw, ctx, inflight, seq) -> list[OrderIntent]:
    c, view, held = ctx.cfg, ctx.view, ctx.port.positions
    orders, nav = [], ctx.nav_liq
    for k in sorted(set(held) | set(tw.w)):
        s = view.get(k)
        if s is None or k in inflight: continue
        pos = held.get(k)
        cur = pos_alpha(pos, s) * s.pool.spot / RAO if pos else 0.0
        tgt = 0.0 if k in tw.force_exit else tw.w.get(k, 0.0) * nav
        if tw.halt and tgt > cur: tgt = cur                         # halted: never add risk
        band = max(c.min_order_tao, c.rebalance_band * tgt)
        urgent, oid = k in tw.force_exit, f"{ctx.raw.block}-{seq + len(orders)}"
        if pos and tgt == 0.0:                                      # full exit (full_exit=True: exempt from partial-sell minimums)
            a = pos_alpha(pos, s)
            orders.append(OrderIntent(oid, k, "sell", pos.hotkey, a, _sell_limit(s.pool, a, 0.15 if urgent else 0.03),
                                      True, True, ctx.raw.block, 8, "risk_exit" if urgent else "exit"))
        elif tgt - cur > band:                                      # buy; never below 2x the 0.002-TAO minimum stake
            hk = pos.hotkey if pos else pick_hotkey(s, ctx.feats[k].best_hotkey if k in ctx.feats else None)
            if hk is None or not s.subtoken_enabled: continue
            spend = min(int((tgt - cur) * RAO), ctx.port.cash)
            if spend < amm.MIN_STAKE * 2: continue
            orders.append(OrderIntent(oid, k, "buy", hk, spend, _buy_limit(s.pool, spend, 0.01), False, False,
                                      ctx.raw.block, 8, tw.why.get(k, "rebalance")))
        elif pos and cur - tgt > band:                              # trim, keeping a remainder above the 0.02-TAO nominator-dust floor
            a = int((cur - tgt) / s.pool.spot * RAO)
            if a * s.pool.spot / RAO >= 0.02 and (cur - tgt) / cur < 0.999:
                orders.append(OrderIntent(oid, k, "sell", pos.hotkey, a, _sell_limit(s.pool, a, 0.03), False, False,
                                          ctx.raw.block, 8, "trim"))
    return orders

def emission_shares(snap, eligible_flag=None, block_tao=0.5) -> dict[SubnetKey, tuple[float, float]]:
    """Re-implementation of coinbase get_shares (brief 3.2). Returns {key: (tao_per_block, gate_keep)}.
    gate_keep = g/b = 1 / (1 + (theta/b)^h)."""
    el = [s for s in snap.subnets.values() if s.first_emission_block is not None and s.subtoken_enabled and s.reg_allowed
          and (eligible_flag is None or eligible_flag.get(s.key.netuid, True))]
    tot = sum(s.ema for s in el)
    if tot <= 0: return {}
    sh = {s.key: s.ema / tot for s in el}
    b = {s.key: sh[s.key] * (1.0 - min(s.miner_burned, 1.0)) for s in el}
    bt = sum(b.values())
    b = {k: v / bt for k, v in b.items()} if bt > 0 else sh
    th, h = snap.g.gate_bar, snap.g.gate_exponent
    keep = {k: (1.0 / (1.0 + (th / v) ** h) if v > 0 and th > 0 else (1.0 if th <= 0 else 0.0)) for k, v in b.items()}
    g = {k: b[k] * keep[k] for k in b}
    en = {s.key for s in el if s.emission_enabled}            # the gate runs BEFORE disabled subnets are zeroed
    gt = sum(g[k] for k in en)
    if gt <= 0: g, gt = b, sum(b[k] for k in en)
    return {k: ((block_tao * g[k] / gt) if k in en and gt > 0 else 0.0, keep[k]) for k in g}

def ema_alpha(moving_alpha, halving_blocks, blocks_since_start):      # a = SubnetMovingAlpha * b / (b + EMAPriceHalvingBlocks)

    if spot_k >= ema_bottom or a_k <= 0: return None

STRATEGY FAMILIES (each a stateless scorer; sizing is central)
Baselines run as books in the same pass: `cash`, `ew_price` (equal-weight eligible, daily rebalance, price only), `ew_total` (same with the share-price index), `prune_blind` (ew_total without the prune filter, which prices the filter).

1. carry (flow and emission-yield). Own what pays you to hold it when the pay exceeds the leak.
   edge_pd = yield_pd + drift_pd, where drift_pd is the structural price drift: chain-buy bid / pool TAO per day, scaled by gate_keep, minus kappa x (owner + miner sell potential / pool per day). kappa starts at 0.5 as an UNVERIFIED prior and is fitted in the walk-forward training window only.
   Filters: emission_enabled, earning hotkey with take <= 10%, since_start >= 7 days (EMA warm), escrow_frac < 0.25, not in the bottom-4 prune ladder. horizon = 3 days, decide_every = 360 blocks, wake on EMISSION_TOGGLED, PARAM_CHANGED, DEREGISTERED.
   Honest framing: on micro caps the yield is the same inflation that creates the sell pressure (SN70: gate keep 0.003, emission about 0.02 TAO/day, yield about 0.5%/day), so yield is not edge. The report splits every position's P&L into price and yield, so the user sees which part carried the result. Epoch timing is worth at most about 0.03% per order against 0.1% fees, so it is ignored in v1.
2. momo (momentum and rotation). Cross-sectional z of ret_1d and ret_7d (winsorised), long-only top tercile of the eligible universe with pool >= min_pool_tao (default 1,000; the weekly IC was negative in the micro tercile in the Taoflow era). edge_pd = beta_hat x score, with beta_hat a trailing 30-day OLS slope that excludes the last day, floored at 0. horizon 1-2 days, decide_every 600. Variant momo.gate: names ranked 25-45 by burn-adjusted share with a rising EMA rank, using the official elasticity "rank 36 +10% demand -> +26% emission". Rotation via swap_stake_limit (about 0.00125 TAO versus 0.00186 for sell plus buy) is a v1.1 optimisation.
3. fade (mean reversion). Evidence: REV is negative, meaning continuation, so naive "buy yesterday's losers" runs only as a falsification control (fade.naive, weight 0). The live hypothesis is that forced, price-insensitive flow reverts and informed flow does not. v1 trigger: a drop of at least X% in one snapshot that coincides with a cross-sectional burst (>= N subnets dropping together, like the basket-claim bursts of blocks 9.15M-9.19M) or a LARGE_FLOW outflow, with no EMISSION_TOGGLED, no PARAM_CHANGED and no prune-ladder move on that name. Size <= 0.5% of the pool, horizon 1-2 days, stop at -8%. Owner-stake features (to exclude informed dumps like SN15) are v2. Expected outcome: likely disabled by the gates.
4. launch (new subnets). Evidence: day-30 -4.7%, day-60 -57.7%, day-90 -68.3% (0 of 11 positive), 14-day max run-up only +6-9%. So its first job is a risk-overlay universe filter: no new entries until since_start >= min_age unless the launch sleeve owns the name. Its second job is a small test sleeve (default weight 0) on START_CALLED and EMISSION_TOGGLED(True) for young subnets: <= 0.25% of pool, hold <= 7 days, exit when gate_keep < 0.1. It exists to measure the event study at snapshot resolution. First-block sniping is not visible at this resolution, and no claim is made about it.

DESIGN
A small custom reader runs natively on Windows: httpx for stateless JSON-RPC (archive and historical), websockets only for the head subscription. Hashing is xxhash plus hashlib.blake2b. Decoding is about 40 lines of int.from_bytes. One table (SUBNET_ITEMS, GLOBAL_ITEMS) drives key generation, decoding and absent-key defaults, so adding a field is one row. There is no scalecodec and no substrate-interface at runtime. Metadata is needed only to re-derive ValueQuery defaults for a new runtime. That is an optional dev command, and every snapshot records F_DEFAULTED when its spec is outside defaults.DEFAULTS_VALID_SPECS.

def twox128(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    return xxhash.xxh64_intdigest(b, seed=0).to_bytes(8, "little") + xxhash.xxh64_intdigest(b, seed=1).to_bytes(8, "little")
def twox64_concat(b: bytes) -> bytes:

    return p + suffix

def _u(b: bytes, n: int | None = None, signed: bool = False) -> int:

TRANSIENT = {429, -32029, -32004, -32005, -32603}        # rate limited / historical work budget / internal

class HttpRpc:
    def __init__(self, urls, rate=3.0, burst=3, timeout=30.0):
        self.urls, self.i, self.rate, self.burst = urls, 0, rate, burst
        self._tok, self._t, self._lock = float(burst), time.monotonic(), asyncio.Lock()
        self._http = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout, headers={"user-agent": "tao-trader/0"})

    async def _acquire(self):                           # ONE bucket per process: all tasks share the endpoint budget
        async with self._lock:
            while True:
                now = time.monotonic()
                self._tok = min(self.burst, self._tok + (now - self._t) * self.rate); self._t = now
                if self._tok >= 1: self._tok -= 1; return
                await asyncio.sleep((1 - self._tok) / self.rate)

    async def call(self, method, params, retries=6):
        delay = 1.0
        for attempt in range(retries):
            await self._acquire()
            try:
                r = await self._http.post(self.urls[self.i], json={"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": method, "params": params})
                if r.status_code == 429: raise RpcError(429, "http 429", float(r.headers.get("retry-after", delay)))
                j = r.json()
                if "error" in j: raise RpcError(j["error"].get("code", 0), str(j["error"].get("message")))
                return j["result"]
            except (httpx.TransportError, RpcError) as e:
                if isinstance(e, RpcError) and e.code not in TRANSIENT or attempt == retries - 1: raise
                if len(self.urls) > 1: self.i = (self.i + 1) % len(self.urls)    # a different endpoint has a different budget
                await asyncio.sleep((getattr(e, "retry_after", None) or min(60.0, delay)) * (0.5 + random.random()))
                delay *= 2

FILL MODEL (amm.py, sim.py, ledger.py; all tested)
The fill model has four parts: the correct pool, own impact, timing, and failure.
 1. Era-correct pool: the loader hands the simulator an effective PoolState (virtual reserves for the v3 era, Balancer weights for era C). One implementation fits all eras; it matches sim_swap bit-exactly on the cases checked (SN1 live, SN1/19/64 at block 7,000,020).
 2. Own impact as a reserve footprint (SimVenue.foot). The pool the book trades against is the historical pool plus the cumulative reserve displacement of the book's own fills, decayed with a half-life. Two bounding assumptions cover what the rest of the market does with our footprint:
    - permanent (half-life None): the displacement stays. An AMM round trip then costs only fees, because the AMM is path independent. This is the optimistic bound.
    - healed (half-life 0): other flow undoes our displacement before we exit, so impact is paid on both legs. This is the pessimistic bound and the headline number.
    Measured on the prototype, a 10-TAO position in a 1,000-TAO pool loses 0.0119 TAO round trip under permanent and 0.2077 TAO under healed, 17 times more. The truth is between the two and cannot be calibrated before real fills exist, so every report shows both and the promotion gate uses healed.
 3. Timing: an order submitted on the snapshot at block B is eligible at B + latency_blocks (2) and fills against the first snapshot at or after that block, using that snapshot's pool (displaced by our footprint). At 60-block cadence that is one snapshot later, about 12 minutes versus 24 s in reality, which is pessimistic for continuation signals and negligible for 1-7 day horizons. Paper trading uses enforce_ttl=True, so an order older than its 8-block era is "missed".
 4. Failure: limit semantics are strict as in brief 2.6 (a limit at or below spot for a buy raises PriceLimitExceeded; amount above the limit's capacity and not allow_partial is SlippageTooHigh). A failed inner call still pays the transaction fee, so the 1-3% shielded failure rate appears as lost fees, not free retries. Minimum stake (0.002 TAO, plus the post-fee check), the partial-sell minimum, and the 1,000x reserve guards are enforced in amm.py.
Fees: the 0.0504% swap fee per leg is inside amm.py; transaction fees are 0.00103 TAO (buy) and 0.00083 TAO (sell), configurable. Inputs are integers in rao; float exponentiation inside matches the chain to about 1e-7 relative.

MIN_RESERVE, MAX_IN_MULT, MIN_STAKE = 1_000_000, 1_000, 2_000_000
class SwapError(Exception): ...        # .args[0] is the on-chain error name

def buy(p: PoolState, tao_in: int):
    fee = tao_in * p.fee_rate // FEE_DEN
    dy = tao_in - fee
    if tao_in < MIN_STAKE + fee or dy < MIN_STAKE: raise SwapError("AmountTooLow")
    if p.alpha < MIN_RESERVE or dy > MAX_IN_MULT * p.tao: raise SwapError("InsufficientLiquidity")
    e = p.w_quote / (1.0 - p.w_quote)
    out = int(p.alpha * (1.0 - (p.tao / (p.tao + dy)) ** e))
    if not 0 < out < p.alpha: raise SwapError("InsufficientLiquidity")
    return out, fee, PoolState(p.tao + dy, p.alpha - out, p.w_quote, p.fee_rate)

def sell(p: PoolState, alpha_in: int, partial_remaining=False):
    fee_a = alpha_in * p.fee_rate // FEE_DEN
    dx = alpha_in - fee_a
    if p.tao < MIN_RESERVE or dx > MAX_IN_MULT * p.alpha: raise SwapError("InsufficientLiquidity")
    e = (1.0 - p.w_quote) / p.w_quote
    out = int(p.tao * (1.0 - (p.alpha / (p.alpha + dx)) ** e))
    if not 0 < out < p.tao: raise SwapError("InsufficientLiquidity")
    if partial_remaining and out < MIN_STAKE: raise SwapError("AmountTooLow")
    x1, y1 = p.alpha + dx, p.tao - out
    tao_fee = int(y1 * (1.0 - (x1 / (x1 + fee_a)) ** e))        # fee alpha is sold fee-free, TAO goes to the block author
    return out, tao_fee, PoolState(y1 - tao_fee, x1 + fee_a, p.w_quote, p.fee_rate)

def max_buy_to_limit(p, limit):                 # strict: limit must exceed spot
    s = p.spot
    if limit <= s: raise SwapError("PriceLimitExceeded")
    net = p.tao * ((limit / s) ** (1.0 - p.w_quote) - 1.0)
    return int(net * FEE_DEN / (FEE_DEN - p.fee_rate))

def max_sell_to_limit(p, limit):
    s = p.spot
    if limit >= s: raise SwapError("PriceLimitExceeded")
    net = p.alpha * ((s / limit) ** p.w_quote - 1.0)
    return int(net * FEE_DEN / (FEE_DEN - p.fee_rate))

def v_max(pool_tao, slip): return pool_tao * slip / (1.0 - slip)      # exit-slippage budget: V <= T*s/(1-s)

def liq_value(p, alpha):                                              # TAO realised by selling `alpha` now; 0 if it would fail

class SimVenue:
    mode = "sim"
    def __init__(self, latency_blocks=2, heal_half_life=None, buy_tx_fee=1_030_000, sell_tx_fee=830_000, enforce_ttl=False):
        self.latency, self.hl, self.buy_tx, self.sell_tx, self.enforce_ttl = latency_blocks, heal_half_life, buy_tx_fee, sell_tx_fee, enforce_ttl
        self.foot = {}            # SubnetKey -> (d_tao, d_alpha, stamp_block): our cumulative reserve displacement
        self.queue = []           # (eligible_block, OrderIntent)

    def _decay(self, block, stamp):
        if self.hl is None: return 1.0
        return 0.0 if self.hl <= 0 else 0.5 ** ((block - stamp) / self.hl)

    def _displaced(self, p, k, block):
        f = self.foot.get(k)
        if f is None: return p
        d = self._decay(block, f[2])
        return PoolState(max(int(p.tao + d * f[0]), amm.MIN_RESERVE), max(int(p.alpha + d * f[1]), amm.MIN_RESERVE), p.w_quote, p.fee_rate)

    def view(self, raw):
        if not self.foot: return raw
        subs = dict(raw.subnets)
        for k in list(self.foot):
            s = raw.get(k)
            if s is not None: subs[k.netuid] = replace(s, pool=self._displaced(s.pool, k, raw.block))
        return replace(raw, subnets=subs)

    def forget(self, k):                              # generation dissolved: drop footprint and any queued orders
        self.foot.pop(k, None); self.queue = [(b, o) for b, o in self.queue if o.key != k]

    def _add_footprint(self, k, before, after, block):
        f = self.foot.get(k); d = self._decay(block, f[2]) if f else 0.0
        base = (f[0] * d, f[1] * d) if f else (0.0, 0.0)
        self.foot[k] = (base[0] + (after.tao - before.tao), base[1] + (after.alpha - before.alpha), block)

    async def submit(self, orders, snap):
        for o in orders: self.queue.append((snap.block + self.latency, o))

    async def poll(self, snap, held):                 # `snap` is already the book's view
        due = [(b, o) for b, o in self.queue if b <= snap.block]
        self.queue = [(b, o) for b, o in self.queue if b > snap.block]
        return [self._fill(o, snap, held) for _, o in due]

    def _fill(self, o, snap, held):
        s = snap.get(o.key); tx = self.buy_tx if o.side == "buy" else self.sell_tx
        if s is None: return Fill(o.id, o.key, o.side, "pool_gone", snap.block, 0, 0, 0.0, 0, 0, 0.0)
        if self.enforce_ttl and snap.block > o.created_block + o.ttl_blocks:
            return Fill(o.id, o.key, o.side, "missed", snap.block, 0, 0, 0.0, 0, 0, s.pool.spot)
        pool, spot = s.pool, s.pool.spot
        idx = s.hot[o.hotkey].index if o.hotkey in s.hot else 1.0
        fail = lambda why: Fill(o.id, o.key, o.side, why, snap.block, 0, 0, 0.0, 0, tx, spot)   # a failed inner call still pays
        try:
            if o.side == "buy":
                amt, mx = o.amount, amm.max_buy_to_limit(pool, o.limit_price)
                if amt > mx:
                    if not o.allow_partial: raise amm.SwapError("SlippageTooHigh")
                    amt = mx
                out, fee, after = amm.buy(pool, amt)
                self._add_footprint(o.key, pool, after, snap.block)
                return Fill(o.id, o.key, "buy", "ok" if amt == o.amount else "partial", snap.block, amt, out, out / idx, fee, tx, spot)
            pos = held.get(o.key)
            if pos is None: return fail("too_small")
            alpha = int(pos.shares * idx) if o.full_exit else min(o.amount, int(pos.shares * idx))
            mx = amm.max_sell_to_limit(pool, o.limit_price)
            if alpha > mx:

                alpha = mx

            self._add_footprint(o.key, pool, after, snap.block)
            shares = pos.shares if (o.full_exit and alpha >= int(pos.shares * idx)) else alpha / idx
            return Fill(o.id, o.key, "sell", "ok" if alpha == o.amount or o.full_exit else "partial", snap.block, out, alpha, shares, fee, tx, spot)
        except amm.SwapError as e:
            return fail("too_small" if e.args[0] == "AmountTooLow" else

        h, nb = await self.sdk.submit_shielded(o)                                           # Staking proxy; MEV-shielded; era <= 8 blocks
        self.inflight[o.id] = (o, nb, h)

async def poll(self, snap, held):                    # reconcile from POST-STATE, never from StakeAdded or events
    fills = []
    for oid, (o, nb, h) in list(self.inflight.items()):
        if snap.block < nb + 3: continue
        landed = await self.find_inner(h, nb + 1, nb + 8)        # chain_getBlock, blake2b-256 of each extrinsic == inner hash
        if landed is None:
            if snap.block > nb + 10:                              # era (8) expired: the order missed, and that is final
                fills.append(missed(o, snap.block)); del self.inflight[oid]; self.cooldown_until = snap.block + 2
            continue
        alpha0, alpha1 = await self.stake_delta(o, landed - 1, landed)
        tao0, tao1 = await self.free_delta(landed - 1, landed)
        fills.append(fill_from_deltas(o, landed, alpha1 - alpha0, tao1 - tao0))   # zero deltas with the inner found = failed inner call (fee paid)
        del self.inflight[oid]
    return fills

BACKUPS AND RETENTION
 - Market Parquet is regenerable from the archive (about 2 h for era C), but keep one copy: a weekly `robocopy data\market` to another disk. Back up runs.sqlite nightly with `sqlite3 .backup`. Reports are regenerable.
 - Retention: keep per-block recording off by default; record every 60 blocks plus every wake event.

RESOURCES (estimates, to be measured in M2)
 - Collector: 1.7 snapshots/s sustained on the public endpoint (measured); the free OnFinality key (400k RU/day, about 1 RU per request) is ample for Era C. Engine: expected single-digit milliseconds per book-tick for 128 subnets (not yet measured); the 16 threads and 16 GB are far more than needed. A multi-process split is only worth considering if a sweep of hundreds of books becomes the bottleneck.
tradeoffs:
WHAT THE LEAN CHOICES COST, AND WHAT TRIGGERS ADDING COMPLEXITY

1. Custom chain reader instead of the SDK or a SCALE library. Gain: native Windows, five small dependencies, full control of batching, and a 255 KiB single-request snapshot. Cost: we own decode correctness, and runtime upgrades (about every 3 days) can change storage. Mitigation: every decoder has golden fixtures; the collector and paper runs continuously probe against current_alpha_price_all, get_subnet_to_prune and sim_swap and abort or alert on drift; F_DEFAULTED marks specs whose ValueQuery defaults were not validated. Trigger to adopt a heavier codec: more than about 25 storage items, or SCALE structs we cannot hand-decode.

2. Events derived from state diffs, not System.Events. Gain: no metadata-dependent event decoder, identical in backtest and live. Cost: no intra-block ordering and no per-trade detail (so no exact trade-size flow or sandwich detection). Trigger: strategies that need individual trades (Taostats trades or an own archive node, 3.5+ TB, days to sync, per brief 6.4).

3. 60-block snapshot cadence. Gain: the whole of era C is about 2 h of collection and tens of MB. Cost: event-driven reactions faster than about 12 minutes cannot be backtested; the data-cadence contract forbids pretending otherwise. Mitigation: 5-block event windows around known events. Real sub-snapshot evidence can come only from paper and live logs.

4. First-order own-impact model with a bracket. The footprint is additive in reserves, which ignores reflexive responses (other traders reacting to our trades, or emission-share feedback from price). The truth is between permanent and healed, a 17x difference in round-trip cost on a representative position, and it cannot be calibrated until real fills exist. Gain: honest, simple, deterministic; the gate uses the pessimistic bound.

5. Two stores (Parquet for market, SQLite for runs). One more thing to understand, but it removes DuckDB's single-writer problem and gives crash-safe transactional run state. Trigger for a single store: none foreseen at this scale.

6. Single process, single loop. A crash stops everything, and a CPU-bound sweep blocks the feed (not relevant in backtest, where there is no live feed). Mitigations: per-tick checkpoints, Task Scheduler restarts, backtests run as separate processes from the paper trader. Trigger for a split: a slow strategy that makes tick time approach 1 s, or a live book that must not share a process with experiments (use a separate process, which the design already allows).

7. Live adapter on a different OS from the paper trader. The SDK cannot install on native Windows. It costs a second environment and a data sync. It removes any need for a bridge or IPC, and keeps bittensor out of the main process's supply chain. The SDK shape risk (brief 10.1) is contained in one 6-method protocol; FakeSdk makes everything else testable without it.

8. Hand-maintained tables (defaults.py, REGIMES, the registration CDF). The registration CDF comes from 32 observations; regimes and defaults change with governance. Mitigation: params are read live where possible, spec changes halt new risk until accepted, and the verify command re-derives and diffs defaults when a new spec appears.

9. Tracked hotkeys only. Yield and shares are exact for the 5-10 hotkeys per subnet we track, not for all 40k+. A position can only be opened in a tracked, earning hotkey (otherwise plan skips it, as it cannot value the position). Measured spread across hotkeys on SN70 was only about 0.05%/day, so this loses little today.

10. Floats in the simulator, integers on chain. Floating exponentiation matches the chain to about 1e-7 relative (bit-exact in the cases checked), but integer floors can differ by a few rao. Acceptable for backtests; the live path uses chain post-state, never model output, for accounting.

11. Evidence limits that no architecture fixes. The gate-era sample is about 66-109 days. Dereg payouts are formula-based until a real dissolution is replayed (brief 10.10). Yield-versus-dilution netting on micro caps is exactly the unresolved sign in the brief. Capacity is tiny (brief: positions beyond about 1-2% of the pool's TAO reserve are not executable at acceptable slippage). The system makes these visible; it does not remove them.

12. Things deliberately postponed. Swap-based rotation (swap_stake_limit), exit tranching beyond a simple per-tick limit, epoch-timing of entries (worth at most about 0.03% per order), owner-stake and conviction features for informed-dump detection, a delayed-NonTransfer manager proxy, multi-delegate rotation (untested, brief 5.9), a Taostats-driven volume feature, and a System.Events decoder. Each is additive: none requires changing the core types.

13. Regulatory and advice boundary. Outputs describe what backtests and paper trading show on historical data. Nothing here is personalised investment or tax advice (tax treatment of staking rewards is an open question in the brief, with per-epoch lot records recommended).

14. Honest default. If the gates are not met, the correct output of this system is "hold TAO", and the tooling is built so that outcome is cheap to reach and easy to defend.

name: Journal-First Deterministic Core: an event-sourced, replay-identical engine for micro-cap dTAO alpha trading
philosophy:
THESIS. This is a research instrument first and a trading bot second. The evidence in the brief is mostly negative or ambiguous: gate-era micro-cap price-only longs lose about 0.5%/day, nominator yield of 0.3-0.6%/day may or may not offset that, seeded launches fall 68-74% by day 90, and a prune returns 0.35-0.65x spot. A system that cannot be trusted to replay, reconcile and fail closed will produce believable but wrong numbers about money. So correctness of money handling and reproducibility come before features.

CORE IDEA: ONE ENGINE, THREE SHELLS (functional core, imperative shell)
- `reduce(state, event) -> state` is a pure fold. It is the only way state changes.
- `Engine.decide(state, input, snapshot) -> list[Event]` is a deterministic function: derive chain events, account (dereg and yield), run strategies, allocate, apply risk overlays, plan orders.
- The `Runner` loop is the only code with side effects. It is identical in backtest, paper and live. Modes differ ONLY in the adapters handed to its constructor: `DataSource` (lake / live finalized feed / journal), `ExecutionVenue` (sim / paper / live SDK), `Journal` backend (memory / SQLite). The engine package contains no `if mode ==` branch. Own market impact is applied at the data boundary via `venue.mark_to(snapshot)`: SIM and PAPER add an overlay of our own flows, LIVE returns the snapshot unchanged because the chain already contains our trades.

TEN RULES
1. The append-only, hash-chained journal is the single source of truth for state. Memory is a cache that can always be rebuilt by replay.
2. Atomic batch commit: an input event and every decision derived from it are written in ONE SQLite transaction (WAL, synchronous=FULL). Side effects happen strictly AFTER commit. This is the only crash-safety mechanism, and it is small enough to verify exhaustively.
3. Every order goes through a write-ahead bracket: `OrderIntended` (the outbox record), then `SubmitStarted`, then the venue call, then `VenueAck` or `OrderFailed`. A crash between steps leaves a state (`SUBMITTING`, `UNKNOWN`) that is resolved from ground truth. It is never blindly re-sent.
4. Identity is deterministic. `order_id = blake2b(run_id, block, subnet generation, hotkey, side, attempt)` and `fill_id = order_id:attempt:leg`. Journal idempotency keys are UNIQUE. A replay reproduces the same ids, so duplicates are structurally impossible.
5. Money is integer rao or exact Decimal, never float. Fractional powers use `decimal` (identical on Windows and Linux, unlike libm `pow`). Floats are allowed only inside strategy feature math and are quantised to integer ppm at the Signal boundary. Units are distinct `NewType`s under `mypy --strict`.
6. Assets are keyed by generation `(netuid, NetworkRegisteredAt)`, never by netuid.
7. The chain is the only truth for balances. In live, positions are reconciled from post-state reads (never from `StakeAdded`). Facts about unknown orders are quarantined and chain truth wins through a `ReconAdjusted` event.
8. Strategies emit declarative targets, not trades, so every tick is idempotent. Risk overlays are monotone: they may only lower a target, add a forced exit, veto an entry or halt. Raising a target raises an exception.
9. Fail closed. Any doubt (spec change, SafeMode, stale feed, model drift, orphan fact, invariant breach) halts entries. Exits stay allowed unless the chain forbids them.
10. Live is physically separate (package extra, Linux only, hash-pinned SDK), off by default, and has a three-stage gate. Nothing in this repo's dev or agent processes ever runs `--submit`.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT BUILD: no microservices, broker, ORM, plugin framework, Rust, ML stack, intra-block simulator, or raw `System.Events` indexer in v1. Events are derived by diffing consecutive finalized snapshots with ONE pure function that runs on both 60-block history and per-block live. A single asyncio process and two embedded databases are enough.

VALIDATED BY A WORKING PROTOTYPE (not just a paper design). Location: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-USER-Trading\078f8f5d-bbc4-4198-bd72-fb11df99d05a\scratchpad\jf_proto (src\stq, tests). About 1,900 source lines, 16 modules, `mypy --strict` clean, 32 tests passing in about 37 s on this Windows host with Python 3.11. Results:
- AMM: SN1 fee vector (503,547 rao on 1 TAO); SN92 live check (100 TAO into 587.2 TAO gives 63,351 alpha, within 0.1%); property tests that `max_buy_to_limit` never lets the marginal price exceed the limit (balanced and skewed weights); V_max = T*s/(1-s) matches measured exit shortfall.
- Crash recovery: the full 367-point matrix (before commit, inside the transaction, after commit, after SubmitStarted, after venue.submit) was crashed one point at a time, restarted with brand-new objects, and reached the byte-identical final money-state digest in 367 of 367 cases, with no duplicate fills or intents. pytest samples about 140 of those points; the rest ran in a standalone script.
- Determinism: two runs give byte-identical journal hash chains; a restart on a complete journal re-verifies every decision and re-journals nothing; results are identical under PYTHONHASHSEED 1, 777 and 0.
- Key hashing: `twox128("System")`, `System.Account` and `Timestamp.Now` prefixes match the known Substrate vectors using xxhash on Windows. U64F64, U96F32 and SafeFloat decoding is bit-exact (hypothesis).
- Measured cost: `decide` is about 0.4 ms per tick at 128 subnets (no positions); a full 128-subnet snapshot digest is 4.5 ms, so digests are precomputed and stored.

BUGS THE PROTOTYPE CAUGHT (each is now a design rule):
(a) `Decimal.normalize()` rounds to the 28-digit context precision and silently corrupted share counts in the journal. Replay verification caught it. The codec uses exact `format(d, 'f')` text.
(b) Applying a fill before the same block's yield accrual left the position ledger negative. The snapshot batch (derive, account, decide) must commit before fills due at that block.
(c) A CRITICAL exit with a fill-or-kill 2% limit was rejected every tick while the price bled until the subnet was removed. Exit limits are now tied to the dereg counterfactual and CRITICAL exits may part-fill.
(d) If the venue returns several fills computed against the same pre-trade pool, a crash-restarted run diverges from an uncrashed one. The venue returns one event per poll and the runner re-polls with the updated own-impact overlay.

EVIDENCE-HONEST BY CONSTRUCTION. Reports always include null benchmarks (hold TAO; equal-weight micro-cap hold on total return; random-entry with identical turnover and sizing), effective sample sizes and regime splits, and print 'insufficient evidence' where n is small (gate era is only about 72-109 days; launch cohort n=11). This system never gives personalized investment advice. It reports what backtests and paper trading show, and every report template carries that statement.

event_flow:
ONE LOOP, THREE MODES. Everything below is the tested `Runner`/`Engine` code path.

```
 DataSource (adapter)            Runner tick (identical everywhere)                              ExecutionVenue (adapter)
 HistoricalSource(lake)  --+
 LiveChainFeed(finalized)  +--> SourceItem(raw snapshot)
 JournalSource(recovery) --+        |
                                    v
   1. obs = SnapshotObserved(block, hash, digest)                        [input; payload stays in the lake]
   2. outs = Engine.decide(state, obs, venue.mark_to(raw))               [PURE; nothing external has happened]
        INGEST : derive_events(prev, cur) -> SubnetRegistered / SubnetRemoved / EmissionEnabledChanged / EpochDrained / SpecVersionChanged
        ACCOUNT: DeregSettled (uses the LAST GOOD snapshot) ; YieldAccrued (index catch-up per held position)
        DECIDE : strategies (cadence or event trigger) -> standing Signals -> Allocator (sleeves, attribution)
                 -> RiskOverlay chain (monotone) -> TargetWeights -> Planner (pool caps, V_max, limits, min-order)
        EMIT   : DecisionTrace + OrderIntended*
   3. journal.append_batch([obs, *outs])                                 [ATOMIC + fsync = THE COMMIT POINT]
   4. for e in batch: state = reduce(state, e); venue.observe(e)         [memory follows the journal, never leads it]
   5. loop: evs = venue.advance(venue.mark_to(raw)); commit evs[0]       [fills due NOW, ONE at a time, each its own batch]
   6. flush_outbox(): INTENDED -> commit SubmitStarted -> venue.submit -> commit VenueAck | OrderFailed
```
Phase ordering inside a tick is fixed (INGEST, ACCOUNT, DECIDE, EMIT, then VENUE). Fills due at block b are applied AFTER the block-b snapshot batch, so yield for block b is accrued before a fill changes the share count (bug (b) in the prototype). Decisions at b therefore see fills from b-1 and earlier; the position lock (`busy(key, hotkey)`) prevents duplicate orders in the gap.

The runner core (tested):
```python
async def _commit(self, t, ev, snap):
    k = ev.idem()
    if k is not None and self.journal.has_idem(k): return                  # idempotent re-delivery: drop silently
    outs = self.engine.decide(self.state, ev, snap)                        # pure
    batch = [(LogicalTime(t.block, t.phase, 0), ev)] + [(LogicalTime(t.block, phase_of(o), n + 1), o) for n, o in enumerate(outs)]
    self.faults.hit("pre_commit")
    self.journal.append_batch(batch)                                       # commit point (SQLite txn, WAL, synchronous=FULL)
    self.faults.hit("post_commit")
    for _, e in batch:
        self.state = reduce(self.state, e); self.venue.observe(e)
    check_invariants(self.state.portfolio, self.state.ledger, snap)        # breach => HaltChanged + alert, not a crash loop

async def flush_outbox(self, now):
    for oid, rec in list(self.state.orders):                               # OPEN orders only
        if rec.state is OrderState.INTENDED:
            await self._commit(t, SubmitStarted(oid, rec.intent.attempt), None)      # write-ahead
            try: reply = await self.venue.submit(rec.intent, now)
            except Exception as exc:                                                 # outcome unknown: never blind-retry
                await self._commit(t, SubmitUnknown(oid, rec.intent.attempt, repr(exc)), None); continue
            await self._commit(t, reply, None)                                       # VenueAck | OrderFailed
        elif rec.state in (OrderState.SUBMITTING, OrderState.UNKNOWN):
            res, evs = await self.venue.resolve(rec.intent, now)                     # settle from ground truth
            if res is not Resolution.UNRESOLVABLE_YET:
                for e in evs: await self._commit(t, e, None)

def recover(self):                                  # recovery == the same fold over the journal
    for batch in journal.batches():
        inp, outs = batch[0], batch[1:]
        if isinstance(inp, SnapshotObserved):
            raw = store.get(inp.block); assert raw.digest() == inp.digest         # lake changed since => ReplayDivergence
            redo = engine.decide(state, inp, venue.mark_to(raw))                  # rebuilds strategy/engine caches (prev snapshot, standing signals)
            assert canonical(redo) == canonical(outs)                             # VERIFY mode: code/config drift or nondeterminism is loud
        for e in batch: state = reduce(state, e); venue.observe(e)                # the JOURNAL is authoritative for money state
```
`reduce` is total on valid journals: events about unknown or closed orders increment `orphans` (which blocks new intents) instead of raising, so a live anomaly can never poison-pill the restart loop. Chain truth is then re-imported through `ReconAdjusted` and `QuarantineCleared`.

CRASH WINDOWS (all verified exhaustively in the prototype: 367 of 367 crash points reach the identical money-state digest):

| Crash point | Journal holds | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| before append_batch | nothing | source re-delivers the snapshot; decide recomputes identical outputs |
| inside the SQLite txn | rolled back | same as above |
| after commit, before in-memory fold | full batch | recover() re-folds; outbox re-driven |
| after SubmitStarted | order SUBMITTING | `venue.resolve`: sim/paper re-submit (idempotent, no hidden state); live asks the chain (nonce/era/carrier) |
| after venue.submit, before Ack journaled | SUBMITTING | same; live finds the carrier by delegate nonce and inner hash |
| after VenueAck | SUBMITTED | `venue.observe` rebuilds pending state |
| mid fill-drain | some fills committed | the interrupted tick's venue drain is re-run at the last snapshot before streaming resumes |

IDEMPOTENT ORDER HANDLING, end to end: deterministic `order_id`; UNIQUE journal idem keys (`intent:`, `submit:`, `ack:`, `fill:`, `fail:`); engine position lock (one open order per (generation, hotkey)); write-ahead `SubmitStarted`; explicit `UNKNOWN` state resolved from the chain (mortal eras make every submission eventually decidable: shield eras are 8 blocks); fill ids are `order:attempt:leg`; failed orders put the subnet on a cooldown and a re-decision yields a NEW order id; chain reconciliation is the final arbiter.

DERIVED EVENTS. `derive_events(prev, cur)` is a pure diff and is the only event source in v1. It detects removal (netuid missing or its generation changed), registration, emission flips, epoch drains (`LastEpochBlock` gives the exact drain block), and spec changes. At 60-block history stride and at per-block live it produces the same typed events, so strategies are written against block-time, not tick counts. Raw `System.Events` decoding is an optional later enrichment that needs an archive node and per-spec event maps.

GRANULARITY HONESTY. Backtests run at the lake stride (default 60 blocks, 12 minutes); live runs per finalized block. A strategy must declare its `min_resolution_blocks`; the backtest refuses to run an event-driven strategy at a stride coarser than it claims to support. The live recorder writes per-block snapshots to the same schema, so after weeks of paper trading you can back-test at 1-block resolution on your own data.

STRATEGY FAMILIES AS PLUG-INS (all emit `Signal`s; none knows capital, pools, fees, or venues)

| Family | Triggers | Inputs (all ex-ante) | Posture given the brief's evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) FlowYield | EpochDrained for held and candidate keys; EmissionEnabledChanged; cadence 300 blocks | realised trailing delta-ln(share index) of the best earning hotkey; closed-form yield 2952*(1-rp)/A_earn as a cross-check; take and `earns` flag; gate distance (rank vs theta); dilution drag (owner + miner alpha vs pool); chain-buy support from SubnetTaoFlow deltas; escrow overhang E/x; hard exclusion near the prune ladder | Score = expected net daily return = yield_net + flow drift - dilution - amortised round-trip cost. Must beat HoldTao and the EW micro-cap total-return benchmark or it is reported as no edge. |
| (b) Momentum / rotation | daily cadence (7,200 blocks) plus large-move events | total-return series (price x share index); 1-day continuation and 7-day momentum rank; turnover hysteresis (rotate only if score gain exceeds ~0.19% fees + 0.10% swap + modelled impact) | 1-day and 7-day signals are positive gross in the gate era; 30-day is not significant, so it is not used. Capacity is tiny; sizing is pool-relative. |
| (c) Mean reversion | band breaches of spot vs the fast EMA (600-block half-life), only when no structural event coincides | deviation z-score, EmissionEnabledChanged/rank-cross/owner-sell flags to suppress | REV is negative (continuation) in the evidence, so the prior is that this LOSES. It runs as a competitor and doubles as an anti-chase filter for (b). |
| (d) New launches | SubnetRegistered, start_call (first_emission_block set), EmissionEnabledChanged(true) | cohort tracker: pool at first move, run-up, owner stake, emission state | Default posture is AVOID signals for the first N days (0 of 11 positive by day 90).
